Definition: {a copse of bushes; hence, a forest; hence, honey in the comb (as hived in trees)}
BiblicalUsage: Jonathan heard not his father's charge, so he put forth the end of his rod and dipped it in the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth, and his eyes were enlightened.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the honey in the wood is the picture of provision nobody planned: Jonathan tastes what the forest gives, his eyes clear, and the oath that would have killed him is broken by a sweetness he found by the way.
